summary.headline: Summary of First-Class Mail received per household statistics for fiscal year 2024.

statements.text: For All households, the metric First-Class Mail received per household was 221.7 pieces per household per year in FY2024.
For All households, First-Class Mail received per household decreased by 22.7 pieces per household per year from the previous year across the FY2024 methodology break.
For All households, First-Class Mail received per household fell by 67.1 pieces per household per year from 2019 to FY2024 across the FY2024 methodology break.

caveats: From the FY2024 report, results are published as pieces per household per year, and the survey contractor changed (NuStats to RCF). The FY2024 report restated 2014-2023 on its own basis, so its values for those years can differ slightly from earlier reports (e.g. bills paid by mail in 2014: 34% in FY2023, 33% in FY2024).
Beginning in 2010, diary data were restated because of changes in weighting methodology (Appendix A8 table notes). Values before 2010 use the earlier weighting.

FY2025 used a new survey design (renamed the Household Mail Survey); Q1 was still covered by the old survey. Age bands changed to Under 45 / 45-64 / 65+ (previously 18-34 / 35-54 / 55+), and 'Large MSA' was redefined in January 2025 from the top 30 metros to metros of 1 million or more.

summary.headline: A long-term comparative analysis of First-Class Mail received per household shows declining volumes alongside drift projections through FY2029.

statements.text: For All households, First-Class Mail received per household fell by 126.5 pieces per household per year from 2014 to 2024, across the FY2024 methodology break.
For All households, First-Class Mail received per household fell by 126.5 pieces per household per year from 10 years earlier, across the FY2024 methodology break.
For All households, First-Class Mail received per household fell by 67.1 pieces per household per year from 2019 to 2024, across the FY2024 methodology break.
For All households, First-Class Mail received per household decreased by 22.7 pieces per household per year from 2023 to 2024, across the FY2024 methodology break.
For All households, the projected First-Class Mail received per household is 209.0 pieces per household per year in 2025, with an 80% prediction interval 201.7 to 216.4.
For All households, the projected First-Class Mail received per household is 196.4 pieces per household per year in 2026, with an 80% prediction interval 185.8 to 207.0.
For All households, the projected First-Class Mail received per household is 158.4 pieces per household per year in 2029, with an 80% prediction interval 142.1 to 174.8.

caveats: Beginning in 2010, diary data were restated because of changes in weighting methodology (Appendix A8 table notes). Values before 2010 use the earlier weighting.

From the FY2024 report, results are published as pieces per household per year, and the survey contractor changed (NuStats to RCF). The FY2024 report restated 2014-2023 on its own basis, so its values for those years can differ slightly from earlier reports (e.g. bills paid by mail in 2014: 34% in FY2023, 33% in FY2024).

FY2025 used a new survey design (renamed the Household Mail Survey); Q1 was still covered by the old survey. Age bands changed to Under 45 / 45-64 / 65+ (previously 18-34 / 35-54 / 55+), and 'Large MSA' was redefined in January 2025 from the top 30 metros to metros of 1 million or more.
